
ADD-BACKGROUND
Add or update Background (user story) section in a feature file

WHEN TO USE
  Use this command to add a Background section containing the user story to a feature file. Background sections provide context for all scenarios in the feature.

PREREQUISITES
  • Feature file must exist in spec/features/ directory

USAGE
  fspec add-background <feature> <text>

ARGUMENTS
  <feature> (required)
    Feature file name or path (e.g., "login" or "spec/features/login.feature")
  <text> (required)
    User story text in format: "As a [role] I want to [action] So that [benefit]"

OPTIONS
  No options available

COMMON PATTERNS
  • User Story Format
    Example: fspec add-background login "As a [role]\nI want to [action]\nSo that [benefit]"
    undefined

  • Update Existing Background
    Example: # Running add-background again replaces the existing Background
fspec add-background login "As a premium user\nI want to login with SSO\nSo that I can use corporate credentials"
    undefined


TYPICAL WORKFLOW
  1. Create feature: fspec create-feature login → 2. Add background: fspec add-background login "As a user..." → 3. Add scenarios → 4. Validate: fspec validate

EXAMPLES
  1. Add user story to login feature
  $ fspec add-background login "As a user\nI want to login securely\nSo that I can access my account"
  ✓ Added background to login

  2. Add background to user-auth feature
  $ fspec add-background user-auth "As a developer\nI want to implement JWT authentication\nSo that users can access protected resources"
  ✓ Added background to user-auth

  3. Add background using full feature path
  $ fspec add-background spec/features/api.feature "As an API consumer\nI want RESTful endpoints\nSo that I can integrate with the system"
  ✓ Added background to spec/features/api.feature

COMMON ERRORS
  ✗ Error: Background text cannot be empty
    Fix: Provide text for the Background section as the second argument

  ✗ Error: Feature file not found: login
    Fix: Ensure the feature file exists in spec/features/ directory. Create with: fspec create-feature login

  ✗ Error: Invalid Gherkin syntax in feature file: ...
    Fix: Feature file has syntax errors. Run: fspec validate spec/features/<feature>.feature

RELATED COMMANDS
  fspec create-feature
  fspec show-feature
  fspec add-scenario
  fspec validate

NOTES
  • Background sections appear before all scenarios in a feature
  • If a Background already exists, it will be replaced
  • Background title is always "User Story"
  • Use \n for multi-line user stories in the command
  • The feature file is validated before and after modification
